paragraphs.text: A plane is a self-contained reality, world, or universe of any size found within the Multiverse of Magic: The Gathering . While planes can be governed by any conceivable set of rules and natural laws, or indeed even inconceivable ones, most planes visited in the storyline are comfortably similar to Earth.
Part of what defines a plane is the behavior of the mana that powers and sustains it.

A plane is a self-contained reality, world, or universe of any size found within the Multiverse of Magic: The Gathering . While planes can be governed by any conceivable set of rules and natural laws, or indeed even inconceivable ones, most planes visited in the storyline are comfortably similar to Earth.

Although planes are sometimes thought to be a separate world occupying the same universe as other planes, each plane is a separate universe in its own right. Except for artificial planes, most, if not all, planes can be considered more akin to alternate realities, with Dominaria — previously the center of the Multiverse — once thought to be the prime reality.
There are almost infinite planes in the Multiverse , separated from each other by the space known as the Blind Eternities , which is filled with chaotic energies, including aether and mana .

Most planes are spheres with an atmosphere and one or more suns and moons; they resemble planets. But there is no law of physics common to all planes of the Multiverse. Planes can be infinite expanses of matter, specks of space, or logic-defying inversions of normal reality. A plane can contain an entire, sprawling universe or nothing at all.

Most planes visited in the storyline are comfortably similar to Earth, spherical worlds with their own orbiting satellites - moons or sometimes even Suns. Other planes may be smaller, like Theros which is as small as a continent; or larger Dominaria contains a solar system with at least 2 other known planets: Jinuoe and Jyr . A large plane can contain multiple worlds such as Kaldheim with its Ten Realms .

Natural planes are naturally occurring worlds that came into existence at some point. Most known planes have one central, populated world, which is typically named after the entire plane. However, it is possible that in vast universes with billions of galaxies and stars, other populated worlds also exist.

A Worldsoul is the aware essence of a plane. One can be hurt magically or manifest itself in various forms. Some magical abilities, such as those of Nissa Revane , may allow communication with a plane's Worldsoul.

There are also artificial planes, worlds created usually by planeswalkers through sheer will (e.g. Serra's Realm ). The creator of such a world defines all of its rules. These planes are unstable and eventually collapse if there is nothing to sustain their existence (like a constant flow of mana, or technical means such as flowstone ). These planes are most likely surrounded by an amount of real space that prevents them from being destroyed by the Blind Eternities. However, this pocket of space eventually wears out, after which the Blind Eternities destroy the plane.

Pocket planes are small "blisters" or artificial constructs that are split off from regular planes. Examples are Agyrem , Metal Island , Urza 's secret room in the Starfield Orb , and possibly Zhalfir before its reemergence. Another example may be the "Eversaloon" of Thunder Junction .

Planes are known to "move" about each other, with some considered closer and further or even adjacent to each other. In particular, the rogue plane of Shadalar is known to "wander an irregular course through the multiverse". A cataclysm on one plane can affect its surrounding worlds, although the occupants of those worlds would not know the cause. Additionally, new planes are constantly created, while others drift out of existence. According to Vivien Reid , each has a different starry sky. Sometimes the stars are colored like a rainbow. Sometimes they move, every night, as though they were giant fireflies.

The Ten Realms of Kaldheim act as mini-planes and are constantly shifting and moving around the World Tree and can even collide. Such an epic event is called a " doomskar " and causes earthquakes, destabilization, and chaos. The plane of Arcavios was also formed by a collision of two planes and still has two suns.

For a majority of the multiverse's history, the inhabitants of most planes had no idea that theirs was not the only universe, or indeed the only world. However, in some parts of the multiverse, non-planeswalkers are aware of the existence of planeswalkers and "have at least a passing familiarity with the idea that there are planes and realities beyond their own".
In the article "Topic Potpourri" , Doug Beyer laid out a framework for the stages of magical civilizations and their levels of understanding magic and the multiverse.
Civilizations of this stage are witness to no magic at all. Hard rules. Facts. Physics. Miracles and the supernatural are dismissed or reduced to scientific laws.
It's not certain if a planeswalker could ignite their spark in a civilization of this stage, but if they do, it may end badly for them.

Magic surrounds the civilization, but its fundamental principles haven't been grasped yet. Fear and superstition abound. There are magical creatures, but few true mages. Magic is a mysterious, unpredictable force. Planeswalkers are unknown—or they blend in with the enigma of magic in general.

In this stage, the civilization grasps the underpinnings of magic. Mana is harnessed, controlled, and applied toward spellcraft. This is magical maturity; many of Magic 's settings have achieved this stage. Taskmages. Great civilizations. Prosperity or strife created due to magic. There may be a few individuals who know of planeswalkers in this stage of civilization, but they're not widely believed; even with mastery of mana, the idea of a multiverse doesn't come readily to the mind.

A civilization comes to understand its world's place, not the center. Planeswalkers are known to disappear and reappear with knowledge of far-off places. However, it's possible that such a civilization still might not understand the concept of a plane . They might grasp that other planets or moons might support life, as their own does. And they might grasp that planeswalkers can visit these other worlds. But the concept that planeswalkers travel through a chaotic void into alternate realities, some of which contain countless worlds within themselves—that is still too weird to comprehend.
paragraphs.section: Stage 3: Knowledge of Planeswalkers and other worlds

paragraphs.text: Civilizations at this point are fully cognizant of the Multiverse model and understand they are only one reality in an infinite universe. Such civilizations further learn about the mechanisms of how planes interact and the practical applications of living in a multiverse.
paragraphs.section: Stage 4: Understanding of other planes and the Blind Eternities

paragraphs.text: A magically advanced civilization developed on the ancient plane of Equilor . Its inhabitants have significant insight on other planes, which leads Urza to seek them out for information on the origin of Phyrexia and the Shard of the Twelve Worlds .

Dominaria has a long history with Planeswalkers and interplanar affairs. The deserts in Jamuraa 's eastern subcontinent are ruled by descendants of immigrants from Rabiah , while Madara 's Clan Umezawa descended from Toshiro Umezawa , who was banished from Kamigawa .
In 4205 A.R., Dominaria faced the First Phyrexian Invasion , including the Rathi Overlay where the artificial plane of Rath was transplanted on top of Dominaria.
As a result, the people of Dominaria had a greater understanding of the existence of other planes that carried on into the Mending Era .

The Strixhaven school of magic on the plane of Arcavios houses the Biblioplex , said to be the largest library in the multiverse. Even before the New Phyrexian Invasion , the Biblioplex contained volumes describing other planes and planar theory.

The Biblioplex's information on other planes is readily accessible to students. Dina researched arcane rituals that would allow planar travel when looking for an ingredient that could not be found on Arcavios. In Omens of Chaos , Bricen notes that "[...] the Bilblioplex is full of books that never made any sense because they're unfinished histories of places we've never been able to go before."

After Jace was appointed the Living Guildpact , Niv-Mizzet appointed Ral Zarek as the Head Researcher for Project Lightning Bug, which was intended to track Jace's movements. This project threatened to reveal the existence of planeswalkers. As a result, Ral and Jace worked together to make the project seem unreliable. However, despite Ral's efforts, Niv-Mizzet learns about the existence of other planes.

Ravnica is later exposed to the wider multiverse during the War of the Spark , when Bolas 's Eternals invaded the plane. The Ten Guilds and citizens of Ravnica found themselves fighting alongside planeswalkers lured to the plane by Bolas's schemes. The defending guilds and Planeswalkers eventually gathered at the Azorius Senate using it as a command center in a counteroffensive against Bolas. After the battle, Niv-Mizzet consulted with representatives of every guild and tasked Ral Zarek, Vraska , and Kaya to hunt down Tezzeret , Dovin Baan , and Liliana Vess , respectively.
The New Phyrexian Invasion saw many of the planes throughout the multiverse get invaded by a force beyond their world.
paragraphs.section: The New Phyrexian Invasion and Omenpath Era

paragraphs.text: In the aftermath of the invasion, Omenpaths persisted between planes, allowing interplanar exchange. In many parts of the multiverse, non-planeswalker inhabitants could now hear about other worlds and travel between them. However, the level of understanding can vary based on plane and relative planar activity. On Eldraine or Ixalan , an interplanar traveler may remain an oddity, while in places like New Capenna or Thunder Junction there is regular travel through the local Omenpaths.
paragraphs.section: The New Phyrexian Invasion and Omenpath Era

paragraphs.text: Before the Great Mending , creatures could travel between planes more easily, and there were multiple means for interplanar travel.

During this time, Planeswalkers were able to bring other creatures with them while planeswalking, such as Urza bringing Xantcha with him on his travels. Planeswalkers, great wizards , and other powerful beings could summon creatures from elsewhere including other planes . The Myojin of Night's Reach also possessed the ability to travel between planes, as well as the ability to banish others (such as Toshiro Umezawa ) from Kamigawa to Dominaria .
Planar links and Planar portals allow travel between planes. Planar portals could be created by Planeswalkers, as well as with technology created by the Thran and the Phyrexians .

While planar portals or transportation by planeswalkers and other powerful beings are the most common means for interplanar travel, there are a few rarer forms. The Skyship Weatherlight was a mighty skyship that could carry a crew between planes.

The Great Mending closed existing planar portals, weakened planeswalkers' ability to bring others with them while planeswalking, and the ability to summon creatures from other planes. For a majority of the period from the Great Mending to the New Phyrexian Invasion , interplanar travel was mostly limited to planeswalkers. Valgavoth could also create doors to other planes to lure victims into Duskmourn , but creating such doors took lots of energy, so Valgavoth did not open them frequently.

In 4560 AR on the plane of Avishkar , Rashmi , an elven aether-seer and inventor, worked on creating a Matter Transporter to show the world what was possible with aether technology. When sharing her findings with Saheeli Rai , a fellow inventor and planeswalker, Saheeli realized that the device may reach into the Blind Eternities and allow travel between planes. Saheeli cautioned Rashmi that continuing to develop the device could have unexpected consequences. However, Saheeli eventually relented and helped Rashmi complete the device.

Rashmi entered the Matter Transporter to the Inventors' Fair , and both inventor and invention were seized by the Consulate during their confiscation of submitted inventions. Tezzeret had Rashmi expand the device into the Planar Bridge , a new planar portal device which allowed large-scale transportation between planes, restricted only by the flaw that it could not safely transport organic matter. In the wake of the Aether Revolt , Tezzeret fled Avishkar with the Planar Bridge. Bolas would later use the Planar Bridge to steal the Immortal Sun and later to transport his army of Eternals during the War of the Spark. Tezzeret would also use the Planar Bridge to transport the Praetors of New Phyrexia between planes, allowing New Phyrexia to set up for the New Phyrexian Invasion .

Elesh Norn sent Vorinclex to the plane of Keldheim to retrieve a sample of tyrite . With this sample, Norn grew and completed Realmbreaker , creating a cosmic tree that could grow out between planes, forming Omenpaths with which New Phyrexia could invade the rest of the multiverse.

Between Realmbreaker's breaching of the multiverse and the detonation of the Filigree Sylex in the Blind Eternities , the multiverse was left scarred in the wake of the Invasion. Along with the Desparking, causing many of the multiverse's planeswalkers to lose their sparks, the Invasion left behind Omenpaths between planes. This allowed a new era where even non-planeswalkers could travel between the planes.
These events also affected Valgavoth's ability to make doors to other planes, as the elder demon required less energy to create his portals after the Invasion.
Planes have their own natural laws and metaphysics. While rare, these different laws may have an impact on planar travelers.

Planeswalkers visiting the plane of Segovia are shrunk down to scale, while creatures summoned from the plane retain their small scale. Invasion of Segovia shows that invading Phyrexians were not scaled down, presumably Omenpath travelers would not be affected either.

Visitors to Bloomburrow are shifted into the form of a creature native to the plane due to a global enchantment. Whether this effect is caused a natural enchantment, the lingering power of an artifact, a Calamity Beast, or some divine condition is unknown. Ral Zarek was turned into an otterfolk when he planeswalked to Bloomburrow. Bello speculates that Dragonhawk was similarly shifted while passing through an Omenpath to the plane.

The planeswalkers Arlinn Kord and Oko appear to be cut off from their home plane's natural cycles when on another plane. On her first planeswalk, Arlinn found out that she did not return to her human form in the morning on another plane. Oko remained in his Lorwyn form after accidently planeswalking away from Lorwyn-Shadowmoor 's daylight side when he first sparked.

The stitcher Geralf Cecani pondered the effects of trans-planar travel on non-planeswalkers in his monograph The Effects of Trans-Planar Relocation on Individual Magical Manifestations . He believed that every plane of existence has its own rules of magic and that every magic user over time will have their magic adapt itself to the natural rules of the new plane. He referred to this process as "naturalization" or "planar acclimatization."
